info.title: Agent Data Tools
info.description: 670 pay-per-call tools for AI agents over HTTP or MCP, from $0.002 a call, most at $0.01. Free calls to start (25 over MCP, 3 over HTTP); then pay per call in USDC via x402 (Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Solana) or by card with prepaid credits from /credits. No account needed; failed calls are never charged; per-tool reliability is public at /status. Crypto: token prices and wallet portfolios from Uniswap v3, chain reads on Base, Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism and Polygon, OFAC sanctions screening. Web: Read public static documentation, pages, PDFs and RSS feeds as clean text, plus link previews and sitemaps. Business: company profiles, domain and email checks. Also Bitcoin, FX, weather, holidays, geocoding, AI text, and JSON, date and validation utilities.
info.x-guidance: Every tool is a GET with query parameters that returns JSON, at /<tool> over HTTP or as an MCP tool at /mcp (same name with / replaced by _), or a smaller MCP server per section: /mcp/prices, chain, web, compliance, ai, everyday, utilities. An unpaid request returns 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header and a WWW-Authenticate: Payment challenge; pay with any x402 client (exact scheme, USDC on Base, Polygon, Arbitrum or Solana) or any MPP client (mppx: evm/charge with USDC on Base, or tempo/charge with USDC.e on Tempo) and retry. Add sample=1 to any tool for a free static example of its output. Failed calls (4xx/5xx) are not charged; AI and screenshot tools return an uncharged 503 when their daily allowance is used up. Per-tool reliability for the last 7 days: /status. Pick by task. Inference and media: /ai/chat (OpenAI-compatible at /v1/chat/completions with tools and streaming, /v1/embeddings, /v1/responses, /v1/images/generations), /ai/chat-large, /ai/embed, /transcribe (speech to text), /ai/speech (text to speech), /image (generation), /describe (vision). Current information: /search, /news. Token or wallet value: /price/token, /price/tokens (up to 20), /wallet/portfolio. Chain state on base, eth, arb, op or polygon: /<chain>/balance, token-balance, token-info, block, gas, tx, receipt, nonce, is-contract, logs. Counterparty checks: /check/counterparty (one call: OFAC SDN, wallet or contract risk and holdings, with a block/review/pass verdict), /sanctions/check (OFAC SDN), /token, /token-report, /wallet-audit, /contract-risk, /x402/check (inspect another x402 seller without paying). Read the web: /extract (page as text or Markdown), /extract/rendered (same, for pages built with JavaScript), /pdf/text, /feed (RSS or Atom), /url/meta (link preview), /sitemap, /summarize, /screenshot. Companies and domains: /company, /domain, /domain-report, /email, /package, /package-audit. Everyday data: /fx, /btc-price, /btc-fees, /weather, /time, /holidays, /geocode, /wikipedia, /dictionary, /papers, /country. AI text: /ai/chat, /ai/summarize-text, /ai/classify, /ai/translate, /ai/embed, /ai/extract-json and more. Utilities: JSON, CSV, encodings, hashes, dates, cron, units and validators. Packs run several tools in one paid call: /pack/token-analysis, /pack/wallet-profile, /pack/website-audit, /pack/email-deliverability and more. Not sure which tool fits a task: GET /find?need=<plain words> is free and names the calls to make (/recommend adds a reranker). Wallets that call often can prepay: GET /credits/usdc/5 with x402 returns an API key worth 5,000 credits, sent as Authorization: Bearer on later calls. Every price is in the 402 answer and in /openapi.json. Start with /guides/web-reading and the bundled Node CLI at /clients/reader/1.7.7/reader-client.mjs; quote needs no key and never signs, while buy requires an explicit cap. Cached examples: /examples/extract/manifest.json. The homepage and llms.txt also include a TypeScript x402 client example pinned to Base, this service's PAY_TO recipient and Base USDC. It caps each payment at $0.01, the ordinary per-call price, so it pays for every tool priced at $0.01 or less. Most tools cost $0.01; a few cost up to $0.04 (each tool lists its price), so raise the cap to call those. Free calls: every caller gets 25 free successful calls over MCP, used automatically before any payment, or 3 over HTTP by adding trial=1 to a GET request (failed calls do not count). Not for the AI, rendering, screenshot, transcription and search tools, nor over HTTP for PDF reading, and at most 2,000 free calls a day in total. When they run out, a card key from /credits continues the same URLs (api_key=adt_… in the URL for clients that cannot set headers). The operator can switch this off. No USDC wallet: buy card credits at https://api.glyphcall.com/credits and send the key as Authorization: Bearer adt_….

post.summary: OpenAI-compatible text to speech (Deepgram Aura-2, MP3 file)
post.description: OpenAI audio speech request shape: send input and a voice, get the MP3 file back as the response body. $0.01 for input up to 300 characters, $0.08 for longer input up to 2,000 characters; the 402 quote for a request states its price. With a prepaid key the charge is 4 credits ($0.004) per started 100 characters, never more than $0.01 up to 300 characters or $0.08 above; the answer's X-Credits-Charged header states it. OpenAI voice names (alloy, ash, coral, echo, fable, nova, onyx, sage, shimmer…) are mapped to Aura-2 voices; Aura-2 voice names work too. English by default, Spanish with language=es. response_format may be mp3 (default), opus, flac, wav or pcm (raw 16-bit, 24 kHz, as OpenAI sends it); opus and flac up to 450 characters; speed and model are accepted and ignored (speaking rate is fixed; X-Note says so when speed was sent). An optional pronunciations object ({"Nginx":"engine x"}) says how to read names and terms. Point an OpenAI SDK at https://api.glyphcall.com/v1 with an x402 or MPP fetch wrapper, or an adt_ prepaid key as apiKey. Failed calls are never charged.

pronunciations.description: Optional: how to say words, e.g. {"Nginx":"engine x"} (whole words, any case, up to 50)

get.description: Check a Base contract before you approve or call it: a low to critical risk tier with named flags (proxy, proxy with no implementation, tiny bytecode, zero token supply), plus bytecode size, the EIP-1967 implementation slot and ERC-20 owner, renounced and paused reads. Unreadable reads are null; EOAs return not-applicable. Limited heuristics, not a full security audit. Use before approving a spender or calling an unfamiliar Base contract. Details: Base contract bytecode size and EIP-1967 slot check (a confirmed zero slot returns isProxy false; an empty/unreadable slot response returns null; RPC failures return 502). A nonzero slot with a zero implementation flags proxy-impl-unset. ERC-20 property reads run only for 500–50,000-byte contracts; individual unsupported/reverting reads are null, while multicall transport failures return 502. Zero supply requires a successful zero read; ownershipRenounced is true only for zero owner, false for nonzero, else null; paused is null if unsupported. Risk tiers are limited bytecode/proxy/zero-supply heuristics, not a full audit; empty slots cannot identify uninitialized proxies. EOAs return not-applicable.

Details: Looks up a pair address on Base through DexScreener and returns the verified DEX, pair URL, token details, liquidity, volume, 24-hour trades, and pair age when supplied by the source. source identifies DexScreener and retrievedAt is the retrieval timestamp. Missing source fields are null; this endpoint does not assess pool security or investment risk. When DexScreener is unavailable, source is Base on-chain: the tokens and DEX (by factory) are read from the pool contract, liquidityUsd is twice the balance of a USD-stablecoin side (null otherwise), and price, volume, trades and age are null. Returns 422 when no matching Base pair is found. Example market values and timestamp are illustrative snapshots, not live guarantees.

get.summary: Scrape website page to Markdown: page URL into clean Markdown or text for LLMs
get.description: Fetch any public web page URL and get clean, LLM-ready text or Markdown: main content, code blocks, tables, links and headings, for RAG and agent context. Static HTML, Markdown or text; optional section ID. Default 20,000 output characters, max 100,000; input 2 MiB. No JavaScript rendering (see /extract/rendered), logins or paywalls. Empty pages, bad sections, browser challenges and errors are not charged. Use to read docs or articles. Details: HTML body details share a 20,000-character budget, independently of primary text/Markdown. Up to 20 code blocks, 20 tables (100 rows/20 cells each), 100 headings and 200 links. Spans/ragged tables use labelled TSV in Markdown; spans are not expanded. HTML code whitespace and list hierarchy are preserved; generated code fences are closed within the output limit. Other Markdown syntax may be incomplete after clipping. Hashes cover the returned hashFormat, not full source. linkBaseUrl reports static source link resolution; supported first HTML base href values are honored, with warnings. Scripts and CSP are not evaluated. Markdown sources retain syntax without structured parsing (warned); sections require HTML. Source content is untrusted. Image alt text is source-provided, not visual interpretation. Images are never fetched; SVG/canvas omissions and missing alt descriptions are warned. SourceMetadata adds unverified author/date declarations with provenance; conflicting/ambiguous values are warned. Separate 2,000-character metadata budget, 5 authors/10 dates. JSON-LD: at most 8 inline scripts, 64 KiB each, 100 graph nodes/depth 8; no external contexts/profiles. HTML complexity: 20,000 elements/128 nested levels. Marker-only source permalink controls (pilcrow/headerlink/permalink classes) are omitted only for same-document ancestor targets, with permalink_controls_omitted. Literal code and ordinary references remain. HTML sup/sub annotations normalize to ^{...}/_{...} in primary output, heading titles and table values with superscript_subscript_normalized; literal pre/code and raw Markdown stay unchanged. This is notation preservation, not general math interpretation.

externalDocs.description: Read a public documentation page for $0.002

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to fetch

parameters.name: maxChars
parameters.description: Maximum characters of body text to return (500-100000, default 20000)

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Returned representation: text (default), markdown, or both. HTML structured details are included in every format; Markdown/plain sources have empty details.

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: Optional visible HTML ID within primary content, 1-500 characters. A leading # (the fragment a docs link shows) or a URL ending in #id is accepted, and so is a heading's visible text when exactly one heading matches (answered with warning section_matched_by_heading). Heading scope includes subsections until next same/higher-level heading; section/article/main/div scope is its subtree. Missing/ambiguous/unsupported targets fail uncharged, and a miss lists the ids the page does offer under sections. A fragment added to url still does not select a section. Leave it out to read the whole page.

sourceMetadata.description: Page-level source declarations, not verified authorship or freshness. Head author/Open Graph date tags and bounded direct Schema.org JSON-LD Article/WebPage-like nodes only; exact-URL matches preferred, otherwise only one identity-free candidate. Author @id references resolve only to unambiguous local Person/Organization names, with both paths recorded. No external context/reference fetching or general JSON-LD expansion. Separate 2000-character value+provenance budget; 5 authors/10 dates. Original date strings are not normalized. Empty for Markdown/plain sources; unrelated entities and ambiguous nodes are omitted with warnings.

linkBaseUrl.description: Effective source-derived HTTP(S) base for links: the first supported HTML base href outside inert/foreign subtrees, otherwise finalUrl. Credentials and non-HTTP(S) base values are ignored with a warning. HTML links/canonical use this base; raw Markdown keeps relative syntax and can be resolved using this field. No linked resource is fetched. This static interpretation does not evaluate scripts or Content Security Policy.

sourceFormat.description: Source interpretation. Markdown is identified by text/markdown, or a .md/.markdown final path served as text/plain (warned). Markdown syntax is retained verbatim within the cap, not converted to HTML or parsed for structured details; text also retains that syntax. HTML section IDs are unsupported for Markdown/plain text.

textLength.description: Full extracted text length before the character cap, within the input limit.

truncated.description: Input or requested primary representation is incomplete. Structured detail limits are reported separately in warnings.

id.description: Source HTML heading ID or direct child anchor ID, when present and supported; not a generated slug.

section.description: Null for full primary-content reading. Otherwise the explicitly requested scope; title/description/canonical remain page-level metadata. Heading scope ends before the next same/higher-level heading, including nested subsections; container scope is its subtree.

get.summary: Web page to Markdown, rendered: a JavaScript-rendered page as text or Markdown
get.description: Same output as /extract, but the page is first rendered in a real browser, so single-page apps and pages that build their content with JavaScript come back with their text instead of an empty shell. Waits for the network to settle (up to 15 seconds). Public pages only; no login. Use when /extract returns EXTRACTION_EMPTY or too little text for a page you can read in a browser.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the page

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: text (default), markdown or both

parameters.name: maxChars
parameters.description: Output limit, 500-100000 characters (default 20000)

parameters.name: section
parameters.description: Optional HTML id to read only that element; a leading #, a URL ending in #id or a unique heading's visible text is accepted

get.summary: Email verification, validation: verify an address with syntax, MX and disposable-address checks, no mail sent
get.description: Check email syntax, DNS and MX records, disposable providers, role addresses, free providers and SPF/DMARC presence. Returns likely-deliverable, risky, undeliverable or invalid with reasons. No message is sent and the mail server is not contacted. These are DNS and syntax signals, not proof that a mailbox exists or accepts delivery. Use before sending mail or saving a signup.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: The email address to check

get.summary: Company data lookup: profile, identifiers and website from Wikidata
get.description: Facts about a company by name or Wikidata ID: official website, founding date, country, headquarters, industries, CEO, founders, parent, employee count, stock tickers and exchanges, and LEI, with Wikidata and Wikipedia links. Public domain data (CC0), best for established and listed companies. No match returns 422, uncharged. Use to enrich leads, vendors and counterparties or ground an answer about a company.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Company name to search for (give name or id)

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Wikidata item ID such as Q60269744, instead of name

get.summary: DNS lookup, WHOIS lookup: DNS, RDAP registration age and email authentication
get.description: Domain intelligence in one call: DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, CAA), DNSSEC status, registrar, registration and expiry dates with domain age in days (RDAP/WHOIS), and email authentication (SPF and DMARC records and policies, whether the domain accepts mail). Use for lead qualification, phishing and trust checks, and deliverability audits. For a trust verdict with named flags use domain_report.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Domain name, e.g. cloudflare.com

get.summary: Domain lookup, trust verdict: age, DNS and email-auth flags
get.description: A trust verdict for any domain in one call: high/medium/low trust with named flags for very new registrations, expiry, missing or weak SPF and DMARC, too few nameservers, no web host and non-resolving domains, plus the key facts (registrar, age, nameservers, DNSSEC). Use for lead qualification, phishing and vendor checks, and before an agent sends mail to or trusts a domain. Signals only, not a guarantee. Raw DNS records: domain.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Domain name, e.g. cloudflare.com

get.summary: Weather forecast: current weather and 48-hour hourly forecast for any city or coordinates
get.description: Current weather by city name, or by latitude and longitude, for any place on Earth: temperature in Celsius, conditions (clear, cloudy, rain, snow), precipitation in mm, wind, humidity, cloud cover and air pressure, plus an hourly forecast for up to 48 hours. Data from the Norwegian Meteorological Institute; city names resolve via Wikidata. Use for travel and event planning, logistics, agriculture and any agent that needs the weather.

parameters.name: city
parameters.description: City or place name, e.g. London or Lisbon (used when lat and lon are not given; with no place at all the answer is for London)

parameters.name: lat
parameters.description: Latitude in decimal degrees, -90 to 90 (with lon, instead of city)

parameters.name: lon
parameters.description: Longitude in decimal degrees, -180 to 180 (with lat, instead of city)

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Hours of hourly forecast to return, 1-48 (default 12; 48 covers tomorrow)

get.summary: GDP by country, World Bank data: current US$, real growth and per capita
get.description: GDP of any country from World Bank data: GDP in current US dollars, annual real GDP growth in % and GDP per capita in US dollars, for the last 1-10 years with the newest year first. Country by ISO code (SE, SWE) or English name. Read from a committed World Bank Open Data snapshot (CC BY 4.0), so every call answers at once; the snapshot date is in the answer. Use for country comparisons, market sizing and macro context.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166 code (SE, SWE) or English country name (Sweden)

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: Years of history to return, 1-10 (default 5)

get.summary: Inflation rate by country: consumer prices, annual % (World Bank)
get.description: Inflation rate of any country: annual % change in consumer prices (CPI) from World Bank data, for the last 1-10 years with the newest year first. Country by ISO code (SE, SWE) or English name. Read from a committed World Bank Open Data snapshot (CC BY 4.0), so every call answers at once; the snapshot date is in the answer. Use for real-return, pricing and macro questions.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166 code (SE, SWE) or English country name (Sweden)

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: Years of history to return, 1-10 (default 5)

get.summary: Population by country: total, growth and urban share (World Bank)
get.description: Population of any country from World Bank data: total population, annual population growth in % and the urban share of the population in %, for the last 1-10 years with the newest year first. Country by ISO code (SE, SWE) or English name. Read from a committed World Bank Open Data snapshot (CC BY 4.0), so every call answers at once; the snapshot date is in the answer. Use for market sizing, per-capita figures and demographics.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166 code (SE, SWE) or English country name (Sweden)

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: Years of history to return, 1-10 (default 5)

get.summary: Unemployment rate by country: total and youth, % of labour force (World Bank)
get.description: Unemployment rate of any country from World Bank data (ILO modelled estimates): total unemployment and youth unemployment (ages 15-24) as % of the labour force, for the last 1-10 years with the newest year first. Country by ISO code (SE, SWE) or English name. Read from a committed World Bank Open Data snapshot (CC BY 4.0), so every call answers at once; the snapshot date is in the answer. Use for labour-market and macro questions.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: ISO 3166 code (SE, SWE) or English country name (Sweden)

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: Years of history to return, 1-10 (default 5)

get.summary: PDF to text, PDF text extraction: extract the text of a PDF document from a URL, page by page
get.description: Extract the text of a public PDF (up to 10 MB) from its URL, page by page, with title, author and page count. Choose the first page, how many pages (up to 200) and maxChars. arXiv abstract links work. If a site blocks our fetch, the Internet Archive's dated copy is read and the answer says so. Scanned, encrypted and non-PDF files fail uncharged. Use to read papers, invoices, reports and manuals into an agent.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute public http(s) URL of the PDF. With no input at all this reads the published sample (the Bitcoin white paper); send url for your own PDF.

parameters.name: firstPage
parameters.description: First page to read (default 1)

parameters.name: pages
parameters.description: How many pages to read (1-200, default 20)

parameters.name: maxChars
parameters.description: Maximum characters of text returned across all pages (1000-200000, default 50000)

get.summary: npm package info, package risk: npm, PyPI, Cargo, Go, Maven or NuGet metadata and dependency-risk signals, latest or pinned version
get.description: Reports package existence, latest version and release, age, version count, npm weekly downloads, licenses, deprecation and known advisory severity. ok means no listed flags, not a safety guarantee. Supports npm, PyPI, Cargo, Go, Maven and NuGet. Optional exact version adds pinned-version metadata and uses deps.dev advisories; use /package-audit for OSV affected ranges and dated FIRST EPSS CVE estimates. Use before adding a dependency.

parameters.name: ecosystem
parameters.description: One of npm, pypi, cargo, go, maven, nuget

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Exact package name, e.g. lodash or @scope/name

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: Optional exact version to inspect; ranges and tags are not accepted

get.summary: Dependency audit: up to 10 packages, exact-version advisories and fixes
get.description: Check up to 10 public dependencies, optionally pinned to exact versions, for advisory IDs, OSV affected/fixed ranges and dated FIRST EPSS CVE estimates. Scoped npm names supported. Detail and subrequest caps apply; omitted details and incomplete coverage are explicit. Missing evidence is unknown, not zero risk. Automated signals, not a safety guarantee. See the buying guide for limits. Use before installing or upgrading dependencies. Details: Audit up to 10 ecosystem:name items, optionally pinned to exact versions; scoped npm names are supported. npm downloads are not queried, unversioned deps.dev detail is capped at one advisory per package, pinned deps.dev detail is skipped, and OSV detail is capped at 15 per request. Batch advisory IDs/counts remain available; omitted details and EPSS coverage are reported. Exact versions add OSV ranges and dated FIRST EPSS estimates for CVE aliases (up to 50 CVEs). EPSS is not a safety guarantee; missing scores are unknown, not zero. Verdicts are bounded signals. Example timestamps are illustrative; bad input is not charged.

externalDocs.description: Dependency audit buying guide and capped client

parameters.name: packages
parameters.description: Comma-separated ecosystem:name items, optionally name@exact-version; max 10. For scoped npm, use npm:@scope/name@version.

get.summary: Sitemap parser, URL extractor: documentation URLs from a bounded XML sitemap
get.description: Sitemap parser: reads one public XML sitemap or sitemap index as structured URLs and source-reported dates. Supports gzip, substring filtering and pagination. Large sitemaps are read from the start (512 KiB, 1000 entries at most, with a warning). Does not crawl pages or follow child sitemaps. Invalid XML and execution errors are not charged; a valid empty match is charged. Use to find which pages of a docs site to read before calling /extract. Details: XML only: the first 512 KiB (a compressed file must itself be under 512 KiB) and at most 1000 entries are read, 60000 XML elements, depth 16, locations up to 2048 characters. DTD declarations are rejected. contains is a case-insensitive substring of source-reported URLs, not semantic search. Pagination counts distinct reported loc values before public-URL validation of the selected page. Returned URLs are not probed; dates are not verified. Index entries are child sitemaps, not pages. DNS-resolution limitations of the public-fetch guard remain.

externalDocs.description: Discover documentation URLs before choosing pages to read

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute public HTTP(S) XML sitemap URL; child sitemaps are not fetched automatically

parameters.name: contains
parameters.description: Optional case-insensitive URL substring, at most 200 characters

parameters.name: maxUrls
parameters.description: Reported matching locations examined in one page (1-100, default 25); invalid/nonpublic locations may reduce returned entries

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Offset into distinct reported matching locations (0-1000, default 0); use nextOffset to continue

lastModified.description: Source-reported value; not a verified modification time.

matchingReportedLocations.description: Distinct reported locations matching contains, before public-URL validation of the selected page.

get.summary: Base wallet balances and account nonce snapshot: see a Base wallet's ETH and token balances and its transaction count
get.description: Base only (all 5 chains: wallet_balances; USD values: wallet_portfolio). An address on Base: ETH and major token balances (USDC, WETH, cbBTC, DAI, USDbC, cbETH, AERO, EURC) plus up to 20 token addresses you pass, the account nonce, and whether it is an EOA, a contract or an EIP-7702 account. The nonce counts outgoing transactions only; not transfer or trading history. Use to check a counterparty's holdings.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Wallet or contract address on Base (0x...)

parameters.name: tokens
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated extra ERC-20 addresses to check (max 20)

get.summary: Summarize web page by URL: fetch a web page by URL and summarize what it says
get.description: Give a URL, get a short summary of the page plus three to six key points, ready to drop into an agent's context. Fetches the page, strips navigation and boilerplate, and summarizes the main text with an LLM. HTML pages only; for a PDF use pdf_text, then ai_summarize_text. Use for research, news triage, link previews and deciding whether a page is worth reading in full. For the full text use extract.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to summarize

get.summary: Website screenshot full page: capture a web page as an image
get.description: Render any public web page in a real headless Chrome browser, with JavaScript executed, and get a JPEG screenshot (1280 px wide, base64) plus the final URL, HTTP status and page title. Set fullPage=true to capture up to 4000 px of page height. Use for visual checks, page previews, monitoring and feeding pages to vision models.

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Absolute http(s) URL of the page to capture

parameters.name: fullPage
parameters.description: Set to true to capture the full page height (max 4000 px) instead of the 1280x800 viewport

get.summary: Bitcoin address balance and activity: check the balance and transactions of a Bitcoin address
get.description: Bitcoin address balance and activity for any mainnet address (legacy, P2SH or bech32): confirmed balance in sats and BTC, unconfirmed pending amount, total received and sent, and transaction counts. Use for payment verification, checking whether a deposit arrived, and wallet monitoring.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: Bitcoin mainnet address (1..., 3... or bc1...)

get.summary: Decode a Lightning invoice: decode a BOLT11 Lightning invoice: amount, description, expiry and payment hash
get.description: Decode a BOLT11 Lightning Network invoice without paying it: network, amount in sats and BTC, description, payment hash, creation time, expiry time and whether it has already expired. Use to check what an invoice asks for before an agent pays it.

parameters.name: invoice
parameters.description: BOLT11 invoice string starting with ln (lnbc... for mainnet)

get.summary: Sourced token and wallet risk indicators with market facts: sourced risk indicators and market facts for a token or wallet before a trade
get.description: Combines the Base token-report risk tier and flags, available DEX market data, and wallet-audit risk tier, flags, account nonce, and native balance. Returns the underlying indicators separately; it does not generate buy/sell recommendations or calibrated confidence, and does not evaluate holder concentration. The account nonce is not full transaction, token-transfer, or trading history. Use as one input before a Base trade.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Token contract address on Base, 0x-prefixed 20-byte hex

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Wallet address to evaluate, 0x-prefixed 20-byte hex

get.summary: MEV and gas cost estimate, Base: estimate Base transaction gas costs under different priority-fee scenarios
get.description: Estimates Base gas costs from current fees and priority-fee presets. Fixed gas units (100k simple, 250k complex, 180k liquidity) are typical assumptions, not transaction-specific estimates or quotes. Valid values: standard, high-mev (3x priority fee), low-gas (half); invalid values return HTTP 400 without charge. No transaction simulation, mempool observation, or MEV/sandwich-risk measurement. Use to budget gas for a Base transaction.

parameters.name: scenario
parameters.description: One of standard, high-mev, low-gas (default: standard)

get.summary: Research papers, Crossref: academic papers search
get.description: Research papers search across journals, conferences, preprints and books (Crossref): title, authors, year, venue, citation count, DOI link and abstract where available. Optional fromYear filter and up to 20 results per call. Use for research agents, literature reviews, fact-checking a claim against published work, and finding the DOI for a citation.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Search terms, a title or a research question (3-300 characters)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of results, 1-20 (default 5)

parameters.name: fromYear
parameters.description: Only works published in or after this year

get.summary: Currency exchange rates, forex: currency converter and conversion
get.description: Foreign exchange rates from the European Central Bank for about 30 major currencies (USD, EUR, GBP, JPY, CHF, SEK, CAD, AUD, CNY, INR, BRL and more). Give a base currency, optionally the target currencies and an amount, and get the rates, the converted amounts and the date the rates apply to. Use for currency conversion, invoice and price calculations, and reporting in another currency.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Base currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code, e.g. USD (an HTTP call with no input at all answers for USD)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated target currency codes, e.g. EUR,GBP; default is all available currencies

parameters.name: amount
parameters.description: Optional amount of the base currency to convert (default 1)

get.summary: Base transaction status and details: check whether a Base transaction succeeded, its sender, value and fee
get.description: Look up any transaction on Base by hash: whether it succeeded, reverted or is still pending, sender and receiver, ETH value, called method id, block number and time, number of confirmations, gas used, gas price and the execution fee paid, and whether it created a contract. Use to confirm that a payment or contract call went through before acting on it.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: Transaction hash on Base: 0x followed by 64 hex characters

get.summary: ERC-20 token approval check on Base: check how much of a token a spender is approved to move on Base
get.description: Check how much of a wallet's ERC-20 token a spender contract is approved to move on Base: the raw and formatted allowance, the token symbol and decimals, and whether the approval is unlimited. Use before a swap or deposit to see if an approve transaction is needed, and to audit a wallet for risky unlimited approvals.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: ERC-20 token contract address on Base (0x...)

parameters.name: owner
parameters.description: Wallet address that holds the token (0x...)

parameters.name: spender
parameters.description: Address allowed to spend, usually a router or protocol contract (0x...)

get.summary: ENS resolve, ENS lookup: ENS name to address and address to ENS name
get.description: ENS resolve and ENS lookup: resolve an Ethereum Name Service name such as vitalik.eth to its wallet address and avatar, or look up the primary ENS name of an address (reverse resolution). Read live from Ethereum mainnet. Use to turn a human-readable name into a payable address, or to show a readable name for a counterparty address.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: An ENS name such as vitalik.eth, or an address (0x...) for reverse lookup

get.summary: Timezone, current time converter: time zone conversion
get.description: The exact current date and time in any IANA time zone (UTC when none is given), with UTC offset, weekday, abbreviation and Unix timestamp, daylight saving time handled. Optionally convert a given moment into up to 10 other time zones in the same call. Use when an agent needs to know what time it is, to schedule across time zones or to turn a timestamp into local time. A bare GET is the smallest paid end-to-end test of an x402 or MPP client.

parameters.name: zone
parameters.description: IANA time zone name, e.g. Europe/Stockholm or America/New_York (default UTC)

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: Optional moment to convert, as ISO 8601 with an offset (default: now)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated time zones to convert the same moment into (max 10)

get.description: Native ETH balance (eth_getBalance) of any 0x wallet address on Base at the latest block, in wei and in ETH. Use to check whether a wallet can pay gas or a transfer; for ERC-20 tokens use base_token_balance, for all holdings at once use wallet_portfolio. A malformed address is rejected with 400, uncharged.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x wallet or contract address

get.description: ERC-20 token balance of a wallet on Base (USDC, USDT, WETH or any token, via balanceOf): raw amount, decimals, symbol and the human-readable amount, live from the token contract. Use to check stablecoin or token holdings before a transfer or trade; for the native coin use base_balance. Both inputs are 0x addresses (40 hex characters); no contract or a non-ERC-20 contract returns 422, uncharged.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Token: a ticker such as USDC, USDT, WETH or DAI, or the 0x ERC-20 contract address

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x wallet address

get.description: Look up the name, symbol, decimals and total supply of an ERC-20 token contract on Base, live from the contract. Use to identify an unknown token address or to format raw amounts; for a holder's balance use base_token_balance. Input is a ticker (USDC, WETH…) or the token's 0x contract address; an address that is not an ERC-20 contract returns 422, uncharged.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Token: a ticker such as USDC or WETH, or the 0x ERC-20 contract address

get.description: Latest block number and block details on Base, or any block by decimal number: hash, timestamp, transaction count, gas used and limit, base fee in gwei and producer. Use for timestamps and confirmation counts; for current fees use base_gas. A block that does not exist yet returns 422, uncharged.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: Block number, or 'latest' (default)

get.description: Transaction receipt on Base (eth_getTransactionReceipt): success or reverted, gas used, effective gas price, fee paid in ETH, number of event logs and any contract created. Use to confirm a payment or call went through; for sender, value and calldata use base_tx. Input is a 0x-prefixed 64-hex hash; a pending or unknown hash returns 422, uncharged.

parameters.name: hash
parameters.description: 0x-prefixed transaction hash (64 hex characters)

get.description: Read the transaction count (nonce) of a 0x address on Base, both confirmed and including pending transactions. Use to build the next transaction or to tell whether an address has ever sent anything; for its balance use base_balance. A malformed address is rejected with 400, uncharged.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x address

get.description: Check whether a 0x address on Base is a smart contract or a plain wallet: bytecode size, whether it is an EIP-1167 minimal proxy and which implementation it points to, and whether it is a wallet that delegates to contract code (EIP-7702; delegatedTo names the code, isContract stays false). Use before sending funds or approving a spender; for a fuller risk verdict use check_counterparty. A malformed address is rejected with 400, uncharged.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x address

get.description: Recent contract event logs on Base (eth_getLogs): the events a contract emitted over the last N blocks (1-1,000, default 50), optionally filtered by topic0 (the 0x 32-byte event signature hash). Returns up to 100 logs with block, transaction hash and topics. Use to watch transfers or contract events; for one transaction's outcome use base_receipt.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x contract address

parameters.name: blocks
parameters.description: How many recent blocks to scan (1-1000, default 50)

parameters.name: topic0
parameters.description: Optional 0x event signature hash to filter by

get.description: List a wallet's recent transfers of one ERC-20 token (default USDC) on Base, in and out, over the last N blocks (1-20,000, default 10,000): direction, counterparty, amount and transaction, newest first, up to 50. Use to confirm a payment arrived or see what was sent; for the current balance use base_token_balance. Malformed addresses are rejected with 400, uncharged.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x wallet or contract address

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Token: a ticker such as USDT or WETH, or the 0x ERC-20 contract (default: USDC on this network)

parameters.name: blocks
parameters.description: How many recent blocks to scan (1-20000, default 10000; Base makes a block every 0.2 s, so 10,000 blocks is about 33 minutes)

get.description: Owner of an NFT on Base: the wallet that holds one ERC-721 token id right now (ownerOf), plus the collection's name and symbol. Use to verify who holds an NFT before a trade, a mint gate or an airdrop; for how many a wallet holds use base_nft_balance, for the token's metadata base_nft_metadata. A missing contract or a token that does not exist is 422, uncharged.

parameters.name: contract
parameters.description: 0x ERC-721 collection contract address

parameters.name: tokenId
parameters.description: Token id, a whole number

get.description: How many NFTs of one ERC-721 collection a wallet holds on Base (balanceOf), with the collection's name and symbol. Use to check a holder before a token-gated action or to see whether a wallet still holds a collection; for who holds one token id use base_nft_owner. Both inputs are 0x addresses; a missing contract or one that is not ERC-721 is 422, uncharged.

parameters.name: contract
parameters.description: 0x ERC-721 collection contract address

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x wallet address

get.description: NFT metadata on Base: the token URI of one ERC-721 token id (tokenURI) and the JSON it points to (name, description, image, attributes), read from data: URIs, https or ipfs:// (through ipfs.io). Strings over 1,000 characters, such as on-chain SVG images, are shortened. Use to show or check what an NFT is; for its owner use base_nft_owner. A token that does not exist is 422, uncharged; unreachable metadata is reported in metadataError.

parameters.name: contract
parameters.description: 0x ERC-721 collection contract address

parameters.name: tokenId
parameters.description: Token id, a whole number

get.description: Read one raw storage slot of a contract on Base (eth_getStorageAt): the 32-byte word, as a number and, when it holds one, as an address. Slot is a decimal index or a 0x 32-byte key (mapping and proxy slots). Use to inspect contract state that has no getter, owners or implementation pointers; for proxies use base_proxy. A malformed address or slot is rejected with 400, uncharged.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x contract address

parameters.name: slot
parameters.description: Slot: a decimal index (0, 1, 2…) or a 0x 32-byte key

get.description: Find the implementation behind a proxy contract on Base: reads the EIP-1967 implementation, beacon and admin slots, EIP-1822 (UUPS), the older OpenZeppelin layout and EIP-1167 minimal-proxy bytecode, and names the kind found. Use before trusting or decoding a contract whose code can be swapped by its admin; for a fuller risk verdict use contract_risk. A malformed address is 400; an address without code is 422, both uncharged.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: 0x contract address

get.description: eth_call: read-only contract call on Base at the latest block, without a transaction or gas: send ABI-encoded calldata, or a function signature such as balanceOf(address) with args and the call is encoded and its result decoded for you. Use to read any view function that has no dedicated tool (the example reads USDC totalSupply). Calldata up to 8 KB; a call that reverts is 422 with the reason, uncharged.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: 0x contract address to call

parameters.name: data

parameters.name: args
parameters.description: Arguments for a function signature in data: comma separated, or a JSON array for arrays and tuples

parameters.name: returns
parameters.description: Result types to decode when data is a signature without them, for example uint256 or address,uint8

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Optional 0x sender address for calls that check msg.sender

get.description: Estimate the gas a transaction would use on Base (eth_estimateGas) and what it would cost at the current gas price, in gas units, gwei and ETH. Give to, plus value in ETH and calldata for a contract call, and the sender when the call depends on it. Use before sending a transaction or to price a batch; for the gas price alone use base_gas. A transaction that would revert is 422 with the reason, uncharged.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: 0x recipient or contract address

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: 0x sender address (default: an empty address)

parameters.name: value

get.description: Check an ISBN-10 or ISBN-13 check digit and convert valid ISBN-10s to ISBN-13. Hyphens and spaces are ignored. Use before cataloguing or ordering books.

parameters.description: The ISBN

parameters.name: bg
parameters.description: Background colour

get.summary: CIDR calculator: calculate the address range, size and netmask of a CIDR block
get.description: Details of an IPv4 network in CIDR notation: network and broadcast address, first and last usable host, netmask, number of addresses, and whether a given IP falls inside. Use for firewall rules and allowlists.

parameters.description: IPv4 network in CIDR notation

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: Optional IPv4 address to test for membership

get.summary: IP address info, classify an IP: tell whether an IP address is public, private, reserved, IPv4 or IPv6
get.description: Classify an IPv4 or IPv6 address without any lookup: version, whether it is private, loopback, link-local, carrier-grade NAT or public, and its integer and reverse-DNS forms (IPv4). Use to triage IPs in logs or allowlists.

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: The IP address

get.description: Semver compare of two semantic versions (1.2.3, pre-releases like 2.0.0-rc.1 handled by the SemVer rules): which is newer, plus the next major, minor and patch versions of the first. Use to decide whether an upgrade is a major change.

parameters.name: token

get.summary: Markdown to HTML: render Markdown text as HTML

parameters.name: markdown

parameters.name: html
parameters.description: The HTML

get.summary: HTTP status code meaning: explain what an HTTP status code means
get.description: Name and plain-language meaning of an HTTP status code (1xx-5xx, including 402 Payment Required and 429 Too Many Requests), and whether to retry. Use when handling API errors.

get.summary: MIME type for a file: find the MIME content type for a file name or extension
get.description: MIME (content) type for a file name or extension, e.g. report.pdf → application/pdf, and whether browsers usually display it inline. Use when uploading or serving files.

get.description: Compound interest on savings or an investment: starting amount, annual rate, years, compounding (yearly, quarterly, monthly or daily) and an optional contribution at the end of each month. parameters.name: principal

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: Measure on this date, YYYY-MM-DD (default today)

parameters.name: weight

parameters.name: height
parameters.description: Height in cm (or inches with units=imperial)

parameters.description: metric (default) or imperial

parameters.name: decode
parameters.description: true to shift back

parameters.name: json
parameters.description: The example JSON

parameters.name: yaml
parameters.description: The YAML text (up to 100 KB)

parameters.name: json
parameters.description: The JSON text (up to 100 KB)

parameters.name: vin

parameters.name: q

parameters.name: author
parameters.description: Search the author only

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Number of works (1-20, default 10)

parameters.name: ip
parameters.description: Public IPv4 or IPv6 address (over HTTP, left out: the caller's own address)

parameters.name: lon1

parameters.name: lat2
parameters.description: Latitude of the second point

parameters.name: lon2
parameters.description: Longitude of the second point

parameters.name: address

parameters.name: type

parameters.name: type

US federal data, public domain; the snapshot's record date is in the answer. Use when an agent needs the current US federal debt figure, its trend, or a daily series for a chart or brief.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: Days of daily history to return, 1-365 (default 30)

get.summary: US Treasury interest rates: average rates on bills, notes, bonds and all federal debt, monthly
get.description: Average interest rates on US Treasury securities by month from the Treasury's Fiscal Data: bills, notes, bonds, TIPS, floating rate notes and the non-marketable series, with totals for marketable, non-marketable and all interest-bearing debt, for the latest month and up to 24 months. US federal data, public domain, from a dated snapshot. Use for the US government's borrowing cost, a rate trend or macro context; not a live yield curve.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: Months of history for the totals, 1-24 (default 12)

parameters.name: security
parameters.description: Optional filter on the security name: bills, notes, bonds, TIPS, floating, marketable…

get.summary: Crypto order book, Hyperliquid: bids, asks, spread and depth of a perp
get.description: Live order book of a Hyperliquid perpetual (BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE…): the best bid and ask levels with price, size and order count, the mid price, the spread in USD and basis points, and the summed depth on each side. Up to 20 levels a side (default 10). Read from Hyperliquid's public API. Use to judge liquidity and slippage before a trade, or for market-making and arbitrage checks.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Coin symbol such as BTC, ETH, SOL or HYPE (default BTC)

parameters.name: levels
parameters.description: Levels per side, 1-20 (default 10)

get.summary: Crypto candles, OHLCV: open, high, low, close and volume of Hyperliquid perps
get.description: Historical price candles (OHLCV) of a Hyperliquid perpetual such as BTC, ETH or SOL: open, high, low, close, volume in coins and trade count per bar, newest last. Intervals 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h, 1d, 1w and more; up to 500 bars (default 50). Read from Hyperliquid's public API. Use for charts, backtests, volatility and trend checks, or as context for a trading agent.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Coin symbol such as BTC, ETH, SOL or HYPE (default BTC)

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Bar length: 1m, 3m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h (default), 2h, 4h, 8h, 12h, 1d, 3d or 1w

parameters.name: bars
parameters.description: Number of bars, 1-500 (default 50)

get.summary: Funding rate history: hourly Hyperliquid perp funding rates and APR
get.description: Past hourly funding rates of a Hyperliquid perpetual (BTC, ETH, SOL…): each rate with its premium and time, plus the average rate and its annualised APR over the window. Up to 500 hours back (default 24). Read from Hyperliquid's public API. Use to compare carry over time, spot funding regime changes, or backtest basis and funding-arbitrage strategies; for the current rate use hyperliquid_market.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Coin symbol such as BTC, ETH, SOL or HYPE (default ETH)

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Hours of history, 1-500 (default 24)

get.summary: Technical indicators, RSI, MACD: moving averages, Bollinger bands and ATR for crypto
get.description: Use when you need technical indicators for a Hyperliquid perpetual (BTC, ETH, SOL…) on closed candles from 1m to 1w: RSI 14, MACD 12/26/9, SMA 20/50/200, EMA 12/26/50, Bollinger bands 20/2 with %B, ATR 14, annualised realised volatility and plain readings such as overbought or above the 200 SMA. Computed from Hyperliquid's public candles; context for a trading agent or dashboard, not investment advice.

parameters.name: coin
parameters.description: Coin symbol such as BTC, ETH, SOL or HYPE (default BTC)

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: Candle length: 1m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, 4h (default), 1d, 1w and others

get.summary: All crypto prices, Hyperliquid: mid prices of every perpetual
get.description: Current mid prices of every Hyperliquid perpetual in one call (BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE and about 200 more), as a coin-to-price map, or only the coins you name. Read live from Hyperliquid's public API. Use for a quick price snapshot of many coins at once, portfolio marks or a price ticker; for funding and open interest use hyperliquid_market.

parameters.name: coins
parameters.description: Optional comma-separated symbols such as BTC,ETH,SOL (default: every perpetual)

parameters.name: address

get.description: Price a European call and put with Black-Scholes-Merton and get delta, gamma, vega (per vol point), theta (per day), rho, d1, d2 and the probability of ending in the money; or give a market price and get the implied volatility. Inputs: spot, strike, expiry date or days, volatility, interest rate and dividend or funding yield in percent. Pure arithmetic, no data source. Use for crypto, stock or FX options, to price a quote or size a hedge.

parameters.name: dividend

parameters.name: outputTokens

parameters.name: limit
